A program checks Feasibility (the two records match and satisfy both participants' private conditions), and an LLM judge checks Integrity (the conversation supports the recorded plan); passing both is a Verified Success. Each scenario has two versions that share the same public context but differ in one private condition, so the correct plan differs between them. Across thirteen LLMs, 36% of conversations rated highly for goal completion fail Verified Success. To learn from outcomes that arrive only at the end of a conversation, we propose Paired-Credit Policy Optimization (PaCPO). After each turn, PaCPO asks the agent for a tentative plan, checks it in both versions of the scenario, and rewards the turns after which the tentative plans fit their respective versions. PaCPO raises Qwen3-8B's Verified Success from 20.4% to 28.3%.

title: SWE-Stream: Scaling Executable Training Data for SWE Agents via Progressive Construction and Elastic Streaming
abstract: Software engineering agents have advanced rapidly, but scaling their training remains constrained by the limited availability of high-quality executable tasks. Development histories contain valuable signals for constructing such tasks, yet they often require substantial reconstruction due to incomplete environments, missing tests, and inconsistent artifacts. We present SWE-Stream, a system for scaling executable SWE training data through progressive construction and elastic streaming execution. SWE-Stream progressively validates and refines task candidates, reusing existing artifacts when possible and applying targeted completion only when necessary. An elastic scheduler asynchronously coordinates construction stages under shared resource constraints, adapting execution budgets based on observed workload demands. Using development histories from 10,728 repositories across six programming languages, SWE-Stream constructs 80,874 validated tasks and collects 118,688 successful trajectories. Fine-tuning Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 on these trajectories achieves resolve rates of 69.0%, 49.3%, and 45.42% on SWE-bench Verified, Multilingual, and Pro, respectively. In a controlled comparison with approximately matched training budgets, SWE-Stream achieves a 45.6% resolve rate on SWE-bench Verified, outperforming three existing data sources. Moreover, its streaming construction strategy improves efficiency, delivering $1.45\times$ the accepted-task throughput of batch construction and accepting 13.2% more tasks than fixed-limit streaming.

title: HEM-Med: A Hierarchical Agentic Memory Framework for Safe Multi-Center Medication Recommendation
abstract: Medication recommendation (MR) is critical for clinical decision support. While existing MR methods are mostly designed for single-center learning, where only one independent hospital is involved, multi-center MR with hospitals of different scales has become increasingly demanding in practice. In multi center settings, abundant data from large medical centers can improve recommendation performance for low-resource centers. Despite a few preliminary attempts on this task, two critical gaps remain. Gap 1: Existing multi-center methods fail to disentangle transferable cross-hospital clinical experience from hospital-specific prescribing patterns, limiting clinical feasibility and physician acceptance. Gap 2: They commonly overlook multi label safety constraints of MR, including drug-drug interaction risks and local formulary feasibility, which are essential for safe real-world deployment. To address these gaps, we propose HEM-Med, a novel hierarchical agentic memory framework for multi-center MR. To address Gap 1, we design a disentangled hierarchical memory module that builds patient-level medication context attribution records and disentangles them into cross hospital experience memory and hospital-specific residual memory. To address Gap 2, we introduce a safety-aware medication set generation module, which integrates dual-level experience retrieval with safety-aware set decoding to produce clinically relevant, safer, and locally adaptive medication recommendations. Experiments on a real-world multi-center eICU dataset show that HEM-Med outperforms representative transfer learning, LLM-based, and MR baselines in terms of both recommendation accuracy and safety.

title: Value-Guided Repulsion for Offline Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Drifting models have emerged as a highly efficient and stable paradigm for policy design in offline reinforcement learning (RL). However, standard drift policies determine repulsion solely from geometric relationships among generated actions and therefore cannot distinguish them by expected value. To address this limitation, we introduce Value-Guided Repulsion Q-Learning (VRQL) to integrate action value estimates into the particle interaction field. For each state, VRQL combines geometric kernel distance with a normalized Q value scaling. This mechanism assigns greater repulsive influence to particles with lower values while strictly retaining attraction toward behavior action. Consequently, this value-guided interaction field aligns behavior regularization with policy improvement without adding an auxiliary behavior model stage. On 50 OGBench task configurations and 6 D4RL AntMaze configurations, VRQL demonstrates highly competitive performance against established baselines, suggesting that value-guided particle interaction is an effective method for offline RL.

title: Cross-Model In-Context Neurofeedback Reveals (Limited) Activation Control in LLMs
abstract: Probes on activation vectors are widely used to detect misbehavior in language models, but their success relies on the assumption that models cannot control what their activations encode. Humans can learn, through neurofeedback, to control the firing of even single neurons, and recent studies investigated whether this ability extends to language models, reaching conflicting conclusions. No experimental design so far disentangles competence at the task from genuine access to one's own activations. We fill this gap with in-context neurofeedback sessions, in which a "subject" model is asked to maximize (or minimize) a score derived from its activations, shown back to it at every turn. In our first experiment, the sentences are generated either by the subject or by a second "writer" model, while the score always derives from the activations of the subject. We test ten open-weight models from five families, with sizes from 9B to 32B. Some models move their own scores considerably, but no more than a writer of comparable competence moves them. Is this because the task requires no privileged access, or because the subject controls its activations while processing the sentences, whoever wrote them? To answer this, we prefill a fixed sentence as the subject's reply at every turn and ask it to increase or decrease the score. Three out of ten models show small but consistent control effects. We further ask whether models can control their activations to the point of fooling an activation monitor. We make models repeat sentences a monitor would flag, such as a deceptive answer for a deception monitor, and ask them to raise or lower the monitor's score. No model learns to lower it, but one model can raise it. In-context control of a model's own activations might not yet be a threat to activation monitors, but it exists in a few models and needs to be tracked as models evolve.

title: Substantial disagreement between satellite- and ground-level nighttime light patterns revealed by SDGSAT-1 and street view imagery
abstract: Over the past three decades, nighttime light (NTL) has become one of the most widely used and powerful proxies for characterizing human activities. Despite the recent proliferation of available NTL data from both satellite- and ground-level sensors, intrinsic differences between these two observation approaches can result in distinct NTL brightness patterns (satellite-ground disagreement). Such disagreement, particularly its spatial heterogeneity, represents a critical yet largely overlooked issue in NTL studies, introducing uncertainty into the interpretation and application of NTL observations. Here, by incorporating SDGSAT-1 glimmer imagery and panoramic nighttime street view imagery with geospatial AI approaches, we present a spatially explicit, wall-to-wall investigation into satellite-ground disagreement across Singapore. Specifically, we characterized citywide disagreement and its variation across land-use types, analyzed contributing factors, and assessed its implications for NTL-based applications, reinforced by Monte Carlo-based uncertainty quantification and sensitivity analyses using independent observations from Singapore and Shenzhen, China. Our study revealed substantial and spatially heterogeneous satellite-ground disagreement across Singapore. Relative disagreement averaged 15% ± 13% citywide but reached 42% ± 12% in 13% of the city. Such pronounced heterogeneity was likewise evident across land-use types, with commercial areas standing out for consistently significant disagreement, where ground-level NTL brightness was 29% ± 26% higher than satellite-level NTL brightness. Building morphology, vegetation canopy cover, and sensor spectral response contributed to satellite-ground disagreement, suggestive of distinct mechanisms underlying the identified patterns. Applying satellite- and ground-level NTL data yielded relative differences of at least 115% and 83% in GDP estimation and NTL exposure inequality assessment, respectively. This study sheds new light on satellite-ground disagreement by moving beyond discrete comparisons toward a comprehensive analysis of its heterogeneity and implications, thereby establishing an empirical basis for integrating NTL observations and contributing to more reliable NTL-based applications and evidence-informed policies on sustainable urbanization.

title: Evaluating multi-satellite VIIRS active fire observations as a burned area proxy across North America
abstract: Wildfire activity fundamentally regulates terrestrial carbon dynamics and atmospheric emissions, necessitating timely and spatially complete mapping of burned area. Traditional reflectance-based burned area products provide robust spatial records but often have multi-week to multi-month processing latencies that limit near-real-time applications. Active-fire detections provide low-latency observations, but their use as a burned area proxy is constrained by temporal sampling gaps and commission errors associated with sub-pixel fire detection. This study represents one of the first applications to use the full three-satellite Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) constellation, comprising S-NPP, NOAA-20, and NOAA-21, to address these limitations. Here, we evaluate how the spatial performance of a cumulative VIIRS active-fire approach varies with temporal sampling, latitude, and fire regime. We developed a VIIRS Cumulative Active Fire (VCAF) approach using the 375-m VIIRS active-fire record across North America from 2012 to 2024, and evaluated its spatial agreement with visually interpreted reference labels and the North American Fire History (NAFH) dataset, using MCD64A1 as a benchmark burned area product. Results from the first full year of the three-satellite configuration (2024) indicate that VCAF had higher spatial agreement than MCD64A1 in parts of the high-latitude domain (>50°N), with particularly high patch-level recall for small reference burned patches (<100 ha) while maintaining high recall for large patches (>1000 ha). The observed performance varied substantially with latitude and fire regime. In high-latitude boreal regions, the greater potential sampling frequency of the VIIRS constellation was associated with lower omission errors and greater spatial completeness in some regions, although environmental conditions such as persistent cloud cover remained important limitations. In contrast, VCAF systematically overestimated burned area in fragmented lower-latitude fire regimes. These results indicate that multi-satellite VIIRS active-fire observations can provide a potentially useful burned area proxy in selected high-latitude fire regimes and highlight the importance of accounting for temporal sampling and fire-regime characteristics when interpreting active-fire-based burned area estimates.

title: Divergent transpiration regulation among 20 urban tree species under extreme heat revealed by UAV multisource remote sensing
abstract: Urban areas face increasing extreme heat risk, yet satellite remote sensing struggles to quantify crown-scale transpiration in heterogeneous urban landscapes. Consequently, species-specific heat responses, key regulatory factors, and tipping points of urban tree transpiration remain poorly understood. Here, we integrated unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) multispectral, thermal infrared, and LiDAR observations with field surveys of 665 trees across 20 species to estimate crown-scale transpiration for nearly 50,000 trees. The UAV-based single-source energy balance model captured diurnal evapotranspiration (ET) dynamics and agreed well with eddy covariance measurements (R 2 = 0.86, RMSE = 0.04 mm h −1 ). At the individual-tree scale, UAV-derived crown-scale transpiration agreed closely with sap-flow-derived transpiration (R 2 = 0.88, RMSE = 0.05 mm h −1 ) and leaf area index (LAI)-upscaled portable-photosynthesis-system transpiration estimates (R 2 = 0.88, RMSE = 0.06 mm h −1 ). Compared with the normal day, landscape ET was higher on the extreme-heat day, mainly reflecting higher tree transpiration (0.47 vs. 0.40 mm h −1 ), whereas grassland and shrub ET remained relatively stable. At the species level, three event-specific response groups were identified: enhanced with significantly higher transpiration under extreme heat (12 species), neutral with no significant change (3 species), and suppressed with significantly reduced transpiration (5 species). Random forest analysis identified the temperature vegetation dryness index (TVDI) and leaf-to-air vapor pressure deficit (VPD L ) as dominant controls of crown-scale transpiration, with tree height (TH) also exerting a strong influence. SHAP-derived tipping points for TH were identified at 7.01, 4.42, and 3.65 m in the enhanced, neutral, and suppressed response groups, respectively. SHAP-derived tipping points for TVDI (0.23–0.34) and VPD L (5.34–5.84 kPa) suggested the transition toward soil-water limitation and atmospheric-demand regulation. Overall, this framework enables spatially explicit assessment of urban tree water use and provides a basis for species selection and irrigation management during extreme heat.

title: DynamicVis: Dynamic visual perception for efficient remote sensing foundation models
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: The continuous advancement of remote sensing technology has enabled high-resolution Earth observation; however, interpreting these expansive images using modern Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) remains a significant challenge. Unlike object-centric natural images, remote sensing imagery is fundamentally characterized by extreme target sparsity and massive spatial redundancy. Key objects of interest (e.g., ships, vehicles, scattered buildings) often occupy less than 1% of the spatial extent, surrounded by vast, target-free backgrounds. Many existing VFMs rely on uniform dense processing (e.g., Vision Transformers), while a substantial branch adopts pixel-reconstruction pre-training paradigms (e.g., Masked Autoencoders). These designs may waste substantial computational capacity on modeling redundant backgrounds and dilute the feature representations of small, sparse targets. To bridge this structural misalignment, we propose DynamicVis , a remote sensing visual foundation model explicitly tailored to spatial sparsity in high-resolution imagery, with a focus on large-scale visual pre-training and transferable spatial representations for diverse downstream perception tasks. Architecturally, DynamicVis introduces a Dynamic Region-Aware State Space Model (SSM) that bypasses uniform computation. It adaptively routes and incrementally models only task-relevant, high-salience tokens while employing a parameter-free integration for background context, drastically reducing the complexity of processing ultra-long 2D token sequences ( ∼ 100,000). Crucially, to equip the network with robust spatial-selection capabilities, we propose a novel weakly supervised Region-Level Meta-Embedding Multi-Instance Learning (MIL) pre-training paradigm. Trained on a million-scale dataset, this paradigm promotes foreground-aware regional discrimination in the latent semantic space, mitigating the semantic ambiguity of conventional pixel-reconstruction methods. Extensive evaluations across nine diverse downstream visual perception tasks reveal that DynamicVis achieves competitive performance across region-, instance-, and pixel-level remote sensing tasks, with particularly strong results in sparse-target and instance-level perception tasks (e.g., small object detection and instance segmentation). Notably, DynamicVis processes high-resolution imagery (2048 × 2048) with merely 97 ms latency and 833 MB of memory consumption without employing any acceleration techniques (approximately 6% and 3% of a base ViT, respectively), offering a favorable trade-off between computational scalability and representation accuracy for multi-granular remote sensing analysis. Source code is available at https://github.com/KyanChen/DynamicVis .

title: Global cross-modal geo-localization: A million-scale dataset and a physical consistency learning framework
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Cross-modal Geo-localization (CMGL) matches ground-level text descriptions with geo-tagged aerial imagery, which is crucial for pedestrian navigation and emergency response. However, existing studies are constrained by narrow geographic coverage and simplistic scene diversity, failing to reflect the immense spatial heterogeneity of global architectural styles and topographic features. To bridge this gap and facilitate universal positioning, we introduce CORE, the first million-scale dataset dedicated to global CMGL. CORE comprises 1,034,786 cross-view images sampled from 225 distinct geographic regions across six continents, offering an unprecedented variety of perspectives in varying environmental conditions and urban layouts. We leverage the zero-shot reasoning of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) to synthesize high-quality scene descriptions rich in discriminative cues. Furthermore, we propose a physical-law-aware network (PLANET) for cross-modal geo-localization. PLANET introduces a novel contrastive learning paradigm to guide textual representations in capturing statistical scene descriptors of satellite imagery. Extensive experiments across varied geographic regions demonstrate that PLANET significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods, establishing a new benchmark for robust, global-scale geo-localization. The dataset and source code will be released at https://github.com/YtH0823/CORE .

title: Physics-driven semantic scattering structure understanding of aircraft target in SAR images
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) has become indispensable for target interpretation owing to its all-day and all-weather observation capability. In SAR target interpretation, electromagnetic scattering information provides a physically grounded cue beyond visual texture and has been widely exploited for target interpretation. However, existing methods remain dominated by local scattering center representations. Such unordered and component-agnostic representations are highly unstable for aircraft targets. As a result, physically existing components with weak scattering responses are often missed, resulting in the incomplete reconstructed topology structure. To address this limitation, we establish Semantic Scattering Structure Understanding as a new paradigm for SAR aircraft interpretation. Semantic scattering keypoints are defined to associate local electromagnetic responses with physically meaningful aircraft components, while visibility-aware attributes are introduced to retain weakly observable yet physically existing components. The keypoints are further organized into a stable semantic scattering structure. Building upon this, we propose S 3 U-SAR, a physics-driven framework to localize semantic scattering keypoints and construct the complete representation constrained by multi-dimensional physical priors, including scattering heterogeneity, rigid-body topology, speckle uncertainty. A confidence-gated joint supervision strategy is further introduced to alleviate optimization conflicts. We construct KP-SAR-Aircraft-1.0, the first fine-grained benchmark for semantic scattering structure understanding. Extensive experiments demonstrate that S 3 U-SAR achieves the best performance compared with baselines. Class-disjoint cross-category and cross-dataset evaluations further verify its generalization capability and transferability. Notably, in downstream orientation estimation, the method improves P 1 ° and P 5 ° by 15.0% and 19.1% over the strongest baselines. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed representation paradigm in advancing SAR target understanding from implicit local response regression toward explicit global structural representation. The trained model and dataset will be available at https://github.com/YYF121/S3U-SAR .

title: Breaking modal barriers: Achieving modality-balanced semantic segmentation across optical and SAR images through optical image-supervised learning
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation

title: GeoSeg-SAM: Task-aligned adaptation of SAM for geological remote sensing interpretation
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: The Segment Anything Model (SAM) has shown strong performance in natural image segmentation. However, its direct transfer to geological environment remote sensing (GERS) is limited by significant domain discrepancies. GERS elements typically exhibit high class diversity, strong inter-class similarity, and imbalanced sample distribution, which challenge SAM’s prompt-driven paradigm in maintaining semantic stability and spatial contextual consistency. To bridge this gap, we propose GeoSeg-SAM, a geological task-aligned adaptation framework built upon SAM. GeoSeg-SAM progressively aligns generic visual features with geology-discriminative semantics through layer-wise semantic adapters, and introduces a dual-scale structure-aware module in the deeper encoder layers to enhance global region-level contextual representation. Meanwhile, the model employs Pyramid Residual Aggregation (PRA) to fuse multi-level geological semantic representations across stages, thereby improving the representational capacity of features. In addition, at the mask prediction stage, decoded features are fused with PRA-based semantic representations using a semantics-constrained fusion decoding strategy, and a single geological semantic token is incorporated to enhance semantic consistency in GERS scenarios. Experimental results on three representative GERS study areas show that GeoSeg-SAM improves mIoU by approximately 3 percentage points or more over the best competing method in each area, confirming its effectiveness in GERS image interpretation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/WanZhan-lucky/GeoSeg-SAM .

title: MCHex: marching cubes based adaptive hexahedral mesh generation with guaranteed positive Jacobian
abstract: Grid-based methods are robust for automatic hexahedral (hex) meshing, but struggle with boundary fidelity and element quality. Conventional pipelines remove outside elements, yielding axis-aligned surfaces converging to the input geometry at first order; subsequent padding and projection are heuristic, offering no guarantees on final boundary fidelity or mesh quality. This paper introduces MCHex, a fundamental reformulation of boundary and mesh-quality handling in grid-based hex meshing. MCHex applies marching cubes (MC) inside each grid cell, ensuring the mesh boundary is an MC surface. The key insight is that constraining cut-cell configurations to 3-regular polyhedra and applying midpoint subdivision produces an all-hex mesh with guaranteed positive Jacobian for every element. MCHex provides three advantages: (1) theoretical positive-Jacobian guarantee for every element; (2) boundary convergence matching MC’s approximation rate, via a non-heuristic algorithm with well-bounded time complexity and the fastest wall-clock time among existing methods; and (3) manifold surfaces for arbitrary geometries plus a natural padded layer. Extensive evaluation on 202 benchmark geometries, using a slightly smaller element budget, compares MCHex with previous state-of-the-art methods; it consistently yields positive-Jacobian meshes with similar boundary fidelity while running significantly faster. It integrates seamlessly with post-processing such as smoothing and simplification, and is suitable for simulation.

title: Exploring Interpretability in Deep Learning-Based Forest Classification - Separating Similar Forest Classes using Sentinel-2 Time Series
abstract: The ecological insurance theory posits that diverse forests are more resilient and better able to adapt to changing environmental conditions. Increasing drought and heat stress in Central Europe promotes mixed forests for maintaining ecosystem services. However, a diverse species distribution complicates remote sensing-based species mapping, as distinguishing pure from mixed species compositions at the pixel level remains challenging. We evaluated the potential of recurrent neural networks (RNNs) for tree-species classification from Sentinel-2 time series and investigated the spectral-temporal features underlying class discrimination, with particular emphasis on separating pure from mixed Norway spruce pixels. We compared RNN classification models with Random Forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and used Integrated Gradients (IG) to quantify feature attributions across spectral bands and time. The best-performing RNN achieved a Macro-F1 score of 0.851 on the test data, outperforming XGBoost by 0.012 and Random Forest by 0.103. Beyond classification performance, the attribution analysis revealed distinct spectral-temporal patterns associated with the separation of pure and mixed Norway spruce pixels. Attribution values increased particularly after approximately day of year (DOY) 125, while B11 showed the strongest contribution during periods of increasing spectral divergence between the two classes. These findings show that recurrent models can provide competitive classification performance while also revealing the phenological periods and spectral regions that are most relevant for distinguishing closely related forest compositions. Combining time-series classification with explainability therefore provides additional insight into the spectral-temporal mechanisms underlying tree-species discrimination and may support more detailed mapping of mixed forest structures.

title: Collaborative Neural Networks significantly Improve Global Aerosol Retrievals From Multi-Angle Polarimeters
abstract: We present the RemoTAP-Hybrid algorithm for global aerosol products retrieved from Multi-Angle Polarimeters (MAP), and apply it to one-year aerosol retrievals from the SPEXone MAP instrument. For the first time, Multiple Collaborated Neural Networks (MCNN) are used to perform global aerosol MAP retrievals over land and ocean. The combined use of MCNN with a full physics inversion in RemoTAP-Hybrid, significantly improves accuracy and computational speed of SPEXone aerosol retrievals. We validate the retrieved Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD), Angstrom Exponent (AE), Single Scattering Albedo (SSA), Absorption AOD (AAOD), Fine mode AOD (FAOD), Coarse mode AOD (CAOD), and fine mode effective radius (reff_fine) with AERONET data. The validation suggests that aerosol retrievals can be further improved when extending the aerosol description to include a fine non-spherical mode. For AOD, the Root-Mean-Square Error (RMSE) is 0.051 (0.037) over land (ocean), while 78.3% (80.8%) of the retrievals are within the requirement formulated by the Global Climate Observing System (GCOS). The RMSE is 0.186 (0.207) for AE, 0.038 (0.044) for SSA, 0.023 (0.014) for AAOD, 0.047 (0.031) for FAOD, 0.043 (0.027) for CAOD, and 0.021 (0.026) for reff_fine over land (ocean). Compared to the current RemoTAP algorithm, RemoTAP-Hybrid shows improved agreement with AERONET for AOD, AE, and FAOD over land and ocean while the number of valid retrievals is increased by 4% (3%) over land (ocean) and the computational time is reduced by 43% (32%). Finally, we present the first global seasonal maps of aerosol optical and microphysical properties and chemical composition from SPEXone.

title: The Gap Is in the Geometry: A Convergent Meta-Analysis of Multi-Facet Aerial and Remote Sensing Video Understanding
abstract: Aerial and remote sensing video is increasingly evaluated like web video, by posing multiple-choice questions to multimodal large language models (MLLMs) over sampled frames and reporting accuracy. This paper argues that this recipe measures the wrong aspect, and supports the claim with a convergent meta-analysis of a broad set of published results, organized in four evidence tiers, in which a claim becomes a position only when collected evidence agrees. Parameter scale exhibits a median of +3.4 accuracy points per tenfold increase on aerial benchmarks, far below a human gap of at least 19 points, whereas acquisition conditions control perception, as 315 of 318 evaluations in 19 within-paper contrasts lose accuracy when conditions such as altitude, view, object size or time horizon become harder. No aerial benchmark in the corpus combines video input with per-task human and random baselines, competence collapses from answering to acting in closed-loop navigation, and the same MLLMs score higher on the aerial benchmark than on ground spatial ones, but lower on studies that test cross-view geometry. From these findings the current study derives five falsifiable principles and proposes the AVU-Card, a reporting card for aerial video benchmarks

title: MonoMIP: Multi-Height Inverse Perspective Mapping for Monocular 3D Object Detection
abstract: Monocular 3D object detection methods increasingly rely on depth-guided transformers, but they operate entirely in the perspective image plane where spatial relationships are distorted by foreshortening. We propose MonoMIP, a dual-decoder framework that adds complementary 3D geometric reasoning through Bird's-Eye View (BEV) features constructed via Multi-Height Inverse Perspective Mapping. We perform IPM at K elevation planes spanning ground to rooftop, producing an ordered stack of height-conditioned metric BEV features that reduces above-ground misprojection and exposes depth-dependent appearance variation across planes. A BEV decoder with multi-scale deformable attention aggregates this multi-height evidence per query, while a depth-guided 3D decoder provides complementary perspective-space predictions. Without extra training data, MonoMIP attains 25.84% Moderate AP3D|R40 on KITTI val and 21.66% on the official test set for Car, outperforming recent published monocular methods on both the KITTI and Waymo benchmarks.

title: The Last Remote Sensing Model Built by Humans? Casting Any Earth Observation Task as Recursive Self-Improvement
abstract: Earth observation (EO) models are still built by hand. For each new task, experts design a training recipe and tune it against a benchmark. We show that this loop can be handed to an agent. Any verifiable task can be cast as a harness and a verifier, where the harness defines what the agent may use and the verifier defines what counts as success. Every EO task can be made verifiable, through labeled benchmarks, independent sensors, physical models or the repeated observation of the same place. Given only these two components, a general-purpose coding agent builds the EO model and improves it recursively on its own outputs. Settings long treated as separate research problems, from learning with a handful of labels to adapting across domains, become choices of harness and verifier. On four EO benchmarks spanning optical, SAR and multispectral time-series imagery, agent-built models surpass the state of the art and keep most of that accuracy from about 1% of the training labels. This establishes a new paradigm for EO, in which people design harnesses and verifiers and agents build the models, so EO models improve as agents do.

title: Trust Before Autonomy: Rethinking Agentic Remote Sensing for Crisis Response
abstract: Agentic remote sensing is evaluated on how many questions it can answer, whereas crisis response depends on whether its answers can be relied on and how much of the decision can safely be handed to the agent. This paper argues that \emph{autonomy should be earned, not assumed}: An Earth-Observation (EO) agent should be granted autonomy in proportion to demonstrated reliability, epistemic honesty and verifiability. The position is supported by an evidential meta-analysis of twelve agentic RS/EO/GIS benchmark studies from peer-reviewed venues. Only one repeats runs, three contain unanswerable tasks and none measures calibration. Their own tables show that completed workflows are often not correct (task success exceeds tool-call correctness by up to 54pp on identical queries), that the gap to an expert trajectory widens overall with trajectory length (from 7 to 56pp), and that capability does not predict abstention (Spearman r from -0.25 to 0.50, all n.s.). The paper then contributes three EO-specific trust properties, an autonomy ladder for crisis EO tasks, and a readiness protocol that replays archived emergency activations before any live use. In this context, current evidence justifies assistive roles only.

title: Context-aware Bayesian Fusion for Multimodal Object Detection
abstract: Reliable detection of pedestrians and road users is essential for the safe operation of autonomous vehicles. However, this task becomes increasingly challenging under adverse environmental conditions, such as poor weather and low lighting, where the performance of state-of-the-art pre-trained object detectors and on-board sensors tends to degrade, which limits their effectiveness and reliability. Moreover, retraining models for each operating context imposes significant constraints due to high data requirements, computational resources, and time. Considering this, we propose a novel context-aware multimodal late fusion approach that integrates a lightweight gating network within our probabilistic calibration framework. The gating network extracts environmental context and dynamically modulates the detection outputs of pre-trained object detectors based on the inferred context, without retraining of the detectors. Our methodology is evaluated on a modified KITTI dataset, in which the camera images and lidar pointclouds are augmented for varying fog levels. Experimental results show that our approach yields an approximately 14% relative improvement over non-adaptive late fusion baselines, achieving a consistent average precision of 56% across different fog levels.

title: CryoTracer: A Synthetic-to-Real System for Filament Instance Tracing in Cryo-EM
abstract: Particle picking in cryo-electron microscopy is commonly formulated as an object-detection problem in which individual particles are represented by bounding boxes, a natural representation for globular particles but a poor match for filaments that can extend across an entire micrograph. Existing methods reconstruct filament trajectories by linking local predictions in a separate post-processing stage, decoupling detection from instance formation and creating potential ambiguities at gaps and crossings. Directly preserving filament identity is particularly useful for polymorphic specimens, where segments originating from the same filament should remain associated. However, learning such instance-level representations is challenging because expert centerline annotations are scarce and costly to obtain. We introduce CryoTracer, a synthetic-to-real framework that addresses this limitation through procedural micrograph generation, transformer-based polyline prediction, and specimen-specific fine-tuning. Procedural pretraining exposes the model to diverse filament geometries, intersections, and imaging conditions before adaptation using a limited number of fully annotated experimental micrographs. CryoTracer represents filaments as ordered centerline polylines and optimizes their geometry using an orientation-invariant discrete Fréchet objective, enabling consistent learning regardless of tracing direction. Evaluation on established and newly expert-annotated datasets shows that CryoTracer improves instance-level filament recovery over existing particle-detection approaches. These results establish end-to-end polyline prediction as a practical alternative to detection-and-linking pipelines for recovering complete filament instances with limited micrograph annotation budgets. Code and data are available at https://github.com/cryotracer/cryotracer

title: Prompt-Segmentation Meets ROI Encryption: Fine-Grained Video Protection Based on Diffusion Isolation
abstract: Region-of-interest (ROI) selective encryption in H.265/HEVC aims to protect sensitive content while preserving the utility of non-ROI regions. Existing coding-unit (CU)-level approaches still suffer from substantial encryption redundancy for two reasons. First, existing approaches map object-detection bounding boxes to CUs, producing regular rectangular regions, which poorly match the shape of irregular ROI boundaries, such as facial contours. Second, their coding-tree-unit (CTU)-based diffusion isolation expands the protected footprint in fixed $64\times64$ blocks, causing encryption-induced distortion to spread over a large number of non-ROI pixels. To address the aforementioned shortcomings, we propose a prompt segmentation-guided CU-level ROI encryption algorithm, which mainly consists of two core components. The first component is a prompt segmentation-guided fine-grained ROI encryption pipeline. It maps pixel-level ROI masks to CUs according to an ROI-overlap threshold, refines boundary CUs to $8\times8$ granularity, and applies format-compliant encryption to multiple syntax elements in the mapped ROI CUs. The second is a dual diffusion isolation strategy to address the encryption diffusion problem. For spatial isolation, the encoder refines non-ROI boundary regions into $8\times8$ CUs and uses PCM mode to bypass intra-frame prediction. For temporal isolation, it removes motion-vector candidates whose reference blocks overlap ROI CUs. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method generates encryption regions that more closely match irregular ROI boundaries, effectively confines distortion to the ROI.

title: $\mathrm{S}^3$-PnP: Plug-and-Play Denoising for Scientific Imaging with Self-Supervised Score Priors
abstract: Modern image restoration methods increasingly rely on large-scale supervised training, yet clean targets are often prohibitively difficult to obtain in scientific imaging modalities such as hyperspectral imaging (HSI) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Plug-and-play ADMM (PnP-ADMM) with pretrained diffusion priors offers a promising alternative, but the learned prior distribution can mismatch both the target scientific image distribution and the distribution of ADMM denoiser inputs induced by dual feedback. To mitigate these mismatches, we propose $\mathrm{S}^3$-PnP, a self-supervised plug-and-play restoration framework that learns a score prior directly from observation-derived ADMM intermediate states, without clean training targets or externally pretrained weights. Specifically, the learned score corrects the input to the analytical prior update, combining observation-driven corrections with analytical regularization. We further analyze the convergence and reconstruction error of the corrected ADMM algorithm assuming an ideal score and quadratic data fidelity. Experiments on reference-guided HSI restoration, single-image HSI denoising, and MRI denoising demonstrate consistent improvements over competing methods.

title: Resource-Efficient 3D Shape and Orientation Estimation of Road Users using Roadside RGB Camera and 3D Radar
abstract: End-to-end deep learning pipelines for camera-radar 3D object detection are well established in driver assistance systems and autonomous vehicles; however, adapting them to roadside-mounted infrastructure presents significant challenges. On vehicles, sensor heights, pitch angles, and relative geometries remain largely uniform, allowing end-to-end models to generalize effectively. On the contrary, roadside sensor installations vary drastically in height, tilt, and field of view across locations, rendering end-to-end models prone to failure and difficult to adapt without massive location-specific datasets. Hence, instead of designing a complex end-to-end pipeline for direct 3D bounding box estimation, a low-cost, resource-efficient two-stage approach is proposed for real-time 3D shape and orientation estimation. The first stage utilizes any off-the-shelf, state-of-the-art method to extract 2D camera bounding boxes and associated 3D radar points for each road user. The proposed second stage then processes these inputs to construct 3D oriented bounding boxes where radar data determines 3D position, predefined templates define size for each road user, and a tiny neural network predicts a site-specific and optimized yaw angle. The algorithm is successfully validated at a curved road with a junction for pedestrians, bicycles, and cars, where it achieves 25 frames per second on an NVIDIA Jetson ORIN for real-time applications.

title: ReDiS: Reasoning-Diagnosis Self-Evolution for Multimodal Reasoning in Remote Sensing
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown strong potential for remote sensing understanding, yet reliable reasoning remains challenging when tasks require fine-grained visual grounding and multi-step inference. Existing approaches typically rely on either costly pre-constructed reasoning trajectories or self-generated signals such as response consistency, which can reinforce shared errors and provide unreliable supervision. We introduce \textbf{Reasoning--Diagnosis Self-Evolution (ReDiS)}, a framework that separates reasoning exploration from candidate evaluation while allowing the two processes to evolve jointly. ReDiS instantiates two role-specific experts from a shared multimodal backbone: a \textbf{Reasoner} that explores diverse visual evidence--answer candidates and a \textbf{Diagnoser} that jointly evaluates the complete candidate set and provides credibility-aware feedback. As the Reasoner evolves, it exposes new candidate distributions and failure modes; the Diagnoser adapts to these changes and, in turn, reshapes the learning signal for subsequent exploration. To handle groups in which all sampled answers are incorrect and group-relative advantages vanish, we further introduce \textbf{Failure-Triggered Recovery (FTR)}, which provides minimal outcome-level correction without prescribing intermediate reasoning trajectories. Experiments on LHRS-Bench, MME-RS, and CHOICE show consistent improvements over Qwen3.5 backbones at 0.8B, 2B, and 4B scales. ReDiS improves category-averaged accuracy by 6.47 percentage points at 0.8B, while ReDiS-4B achieves the highest average performance among the compared remote sensing MLLMs.

title: Hallucination-aware Faithful Reasoning in Remote Sensing
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have demonstrated promising capabilities for remote sensing reasoning, yet they frequently generate visually unsupported reasoning that contradicts the visual evidence. Existing post-training methods optimize primarily for final-answer correctness, providing limited supervision for identifying and correcting hallucinations that arise during the reasoning process. To address this limitation, we propose \textbf{FaithRS}, a hallucination-aware self-reflection framework for faithful reasoning in remote sensing. We first construct \textbf{SFHD-43K}, a dataset of 43K structured, fine-grained hallucination annotations, and train a detector to identify hallucination types, underlying causes, and supporting visual evidence. FaithRS then incorporates this diagnostic feedback into a Safe Detector-Guided Corrective Rollout framework, where a safety-aware gate selectively determines whether and how to revise the response. Training is driven by a composite reward that jointly optimizes answer accuracy, reasoning faithfulness, hallucination reduction, format compliance, and revision safety. Experiments with Qwen3.5 backbones (0.8B, 4B, and 9B) show consistent improvements across four remote sensing benchmarks, with gains of up to 11.64 points.

title: Omni-RS: Unifying Multi-Task Understanding and Generation in Remote Sensing
abstract: Practical remote sensing applications often require both understanding and generation capabilities for the same geographic scene. However, most existing methods address either understanding or generation in isolation, while existing unified remote sensing models' generative ability is limited to text-to-image. To bridge this gap, we propose Omni-RS, a unified framework supporting four remote sensing understanding tasks and five generation tasks. Specifically, we introduce the "Scene-Guided Two-Stage Training" strategy, which first adapts a multimodal large language model to remote sensing understanding and then uses its hidden states to guide a diffusion transformer for image generation. To enable joint learning across diverse generation tasks, we construct UniGen, a unified multi-task generation dataset, by organizing heterogeneous remote sensing data into a unified format. Furthermore, we introduce "Detailed Visual Conditioning", which uses visual conditions encoded by a VAE to guide the generation process, thereby supporting additional generation tasks that require reference images. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Omni-RS performs exceptionally well in understanding tasks and has achieved outstanding results in a variety of generative tasks.

title: Scaling Vision Transformers Without Training: Prune-and-Merge Token Compression
abstract: Vision Transformers achieve strong performance but incur high computational costs from quadratic token interactions. Training-free token reduction methods improve efficiency, but their robustness remains underexplored. We propose Prune-and Merge ViT, a training-free framework for off-the-shelf models. It combines class attention-based pruning with similarity-based merging to reduce redundancy while preserving semantic information. To evaluate robustness we introduce two metrics. Relative Accuracy Drop (RAD) measures relative accuracy degradation under transformations, and Prediction Flip Rate (PFR) quantifies prediction consistency. On pretrained ViT and DeiT, Prune-and-Merge reduces computation competitively while maintaining robustness and better accuracy than existing token reduction methods. Our analysis suggests that hybrid token reduction does not introduce hallucination-like behavior and preserves prediction stability for common image transformations.

title: AI-Enhanced Hyperspectral Imaging for Intraoperative Detection of Low-Grade Glioma: A Clinical Study
abstract: Current image-guided neuronavigation techniques, such as intraoperative MRI and ultrasound, are limited by high costs, limited sensitivity and operational complexity. There is a clear need for more efficient systems to enhance intra-operative tumor detection and improve patient outcomes for intrinsic brain tumor resection. Whereas previous intraoperative brain HSI studies have predominantly investigated high-grade gliomas, glioblastomas, or mixed-grade cohorts, this clinical study focuses specifically on low-grade gliomas (LGGs). LGGs strongly resemble normal brain under white light conditions on the operative microscope. This study characterizes spectral differences between healthy and tumor tissue and provides a paired comparison of HSI- and RGB-based classification at matched tissue locations and under identical patient-level data splits. Tumor regions showed consistently lower reflectance, which may be associated with differences in hemoglobin concentration and oxygenation. A range of classification models was evaluated. The 3D CNN, which integrates spectral and spatial features, achieved the highest median ROC-AUC of 74.5%, compared with 67.9% for the spectral-only XGBoost model and 64.0% for the RGB-based model. These results support further investigation of HSI for low-grade glioma classification and quantify its performance relative to conventional RGB imaging in this cohort.

title: Multimodal Fusion of RGB and Complementary Modalities for Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Multi-modal semantic segmentation adds an auxiliary sensing stream to RGB images (RGB-X), such as thermal, LiDAR, depth, event, polarization, or light field. This can improve robustness in poor lighting and under motion blur. But different sensors often produce features that do not match well, and fusion can become unstable. To alleviate these issues, we propose a bidirectional polarity-aware cross-modality fusion (BPCF) module that effectively captures complementary cues while enhancing feature alignment. We evaluate the framework on six modality pairings: RGB-Thermal, RGB-LiDAR, RGB-Depth, RGB-Event, RGB-Polarization, and RGB-Light Field. Our model achieve state-of-the-art (SOTA) results on eight public datasets, including MFNet, KITTI-360, DELIVER, DDD17, DSEC, MCubeS, ZJU, and UrbanLF. The codes and trained models will be released upon acceptance.

title: Autonomous 3D Visual-Thermal Inspection for Utility-Scale Solar Farms
abstract: Utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) inspection is dominated by aerial surveys, which are effective for identifying module-level hot cells but provide limited visibility of critical components located under the array, including connectors, cabling, fasteners and structural elements. These assets are difficult to inspect consistently at scale, and their defects are often spatially small, partially occluded and difficult to localise from isolated images. We present an automated 3D visual-thermal inspection system (Tricorder) for under-panel PV asset inspection. The approach combines LiDAR-inertial Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) with geometrically calibrated RGB and thermal imagery and machine-learning-based object detection and segmentation. Detected assets are associated with the reconstructed 3D environment, allowing visual and thermal observations from multiple viewpoints to be spatially fused and localised. We demonstrate the approach on utility-scale PV data for MC4 connector detection and connection-state recognition, thermal anomaly identification, and detection of structural components including bolts, nuts and torque tubes. The results demonstrate a pathway from image-based inspection toward spatially grounded autonomous inspection, where defects are detected and linked to specific assets and their 3D locations within the solar farm.

title: DT-LoRA: Reaching Beyond the Tangent Space of Low-Rank Adaptation
abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) often underperforms full fine-tuning. We investigate this performance gap through a tangent-space lens: factorized updates are confined to the tangent space of the current low-rank factors, leaving gradient components outside this space unexploited. An analysis of ten representative LoRA variants reveals that these residual components account for most of the gradient energy and exhibit strong spectral concentration. Motivated by this finding, we propose Dynamic Tangent LoRA (DT-LoRA), which partitions a fixed rank budget into a stable branch and a dynamic branch to capture the principal residual gradient directions. We show that these directions define the optimal update of a local quadratic model under orthogonal-complement and rank constraints. Matrix-free randomized SVD recovers them without materializing the residual gradient, while controlled write-back preserves accumulated updates and stabilizes training within the allocated rank. DT-LoRA adds no trainable parameters or inference cost over LoRA. Experiments across computer vision and natural language processing tasks demonstrate consistent improvements over LoRA and its variants. Moreover, despite being a general-purpose adaptation method, DT-LoRA outperforms task-specific approaches to open-vocabulary domain generalization for semantic segmentation, achieving state-of-the-art results. Code is available at https://github.com/Snipine/DT-LoRA.

title: InSight: A Mobile Assistant Helping Visually Impaired People Navigate Unfamiliar Environment
abstract: Navigating unfamiliar outdoor environments is one of the most demanding everyday tasks for people with visual impairments (PVI). However, existing navigation systems cannot simultaneously satisfy the needs of informative perception and precise localization during navigation. This paper explores the core navigation demands of PVI through a preliminary study. Based on the results of the pre-study, we present the design of InSight, a mobile assistant that combines scene descriptions with precise localization to support PVI navigating unfamiliar outdoor environments. The offline mode of InSight runs entirely on device for real-time navigation, while the online mode streams camera frames to a self-hosted server for arbitrary object detection and accurate localization. Finally, a user study with 21 visually impaired participants validates that InSight could assist users in navigating unfamiliar outdoor environments with increased success rate and confidence compared to mainstream navigation applications like Apple Maps.

title: A decade of summer glacier fronts and calved glacier ice distribution in Kongs- and Krossfjorden, Svalbard, observed by Sentinel-1 extra wide swath
abstract: A statistical method to map atmospheric exposure is applied on the whole decade (2015–2024) of Sentinel-1 summer acquisitions in Extra Wide Swath mode over Kongs- and Krossfjorden on Svalbard. The consistent daily observations not only allow to statistically define a summer glacier front extent of marine-terminating glaciers but also reveal a new application, which is to detect the summer distribution of calved glacier ice, i.e. icebergs, bergy bits and growlers (IBG). These originate from glacier calving during the sea-ice free period. Summer glacier extent that we define statistically as the area where the glacier prevails more than 95% during summer co-locate well with independent glacier fronts digitized from Sentinel-2 optical imagery. Annual summer IBG distributions are classified into percentage ranges of temporal occurrence, representing the proportion of time IBG are detected in the corresponding pixel location. The ten-year record of mean annual summer IBG-occupied areas is compared to separate estimates of summer glacier frontal ablation for the two glaciers Lillehöökbreen and Kronebreen. The comparison indicates a clear link between mean summer calved ice distribution area and the glaciers' frontal ablation with correlation coefficients (r) of 0.67 and 0.85 for Lillehöökbreen and Kronebreen, respectively. Frontal ablation includes both calving and submarine/subaerial melting at the glacier front and combining this with IBG occurrence estimates may provide new insights into the mass loss ratio between calving and melting. However, the relationship between IBG occurrence distribution and frontal ablation appears to be glacier specific. As this study represents a first attempt to map IBG occurrence distribution and mean IBG occupied area and link that to glacier frontal ablation, further studies and application on other glaciers and fjord systems are required to fully assess the potential and limitations of mapping such IBG distribution as a proxy for glacier calving intensities.

title: From national to global: Mapping global center-pivot irrigated cropland with knowledge-guided data augmentation
abstract: Center-pivot irrigated cropland (CPIC) is a large-scale, intensive agricultural irrigation practice with high water-use efficiency. This characteristic enables CPIC to increase crop yields and promote agricultural development, while simultaneously causing groundwater overexploitation and subsequent environmental issues. Mapping the global distribution of CPIC is critical for enhancing water resource management, guiding agricultural policies, and assessing ecological impacts. This study developed a novel methodological framework integrating CPIC prior knowledge into the generation of a global training dataset through designed algorithms, ultimately producing a 2020 global CPIC map (GCMap) based on Landsat imagery. Specifically, we first proposed a shape-prior guided Projection Simulation (PS) to enhance the diversity of national-scale CPIC samples, enabling global CPIC pseudo-label generation through a teacher model. Subsequently, a stratified sampling strategy was implemented to improve sample representativeness across different regions using the pseudo-labels of global CPIC. Furthermore, a dual-temporal correction mechanism was proposed to clean sample labels, ultimately generating high-confidence global training samples. Finally, based on this dataset, a student model was trained using a noise-resistant loss function and deployed on cloud computing platforms to generate the GCMap rapidly. Following Olofsson's design-based stratified sampling and error-matrix framework, we derived statistically rigorous area estimates with explicit 95% confidence intervals and assessed mapping accuracy using the corresponding user's accuracy (UA), producer's accuracy (PA), and overall accuracy (OA) metrics. In comparison with current CPIC products, our GCMap attained a PA of 0.86 ± 0.02, representing a marked reduction in omission errors. Our results show that the global error-adjusted area of CPIC in 2020 was estimated at 18.70 ± 0.42 Mha, representing a 63% increase relative to the previous estimate of 11.5 Mha and revealing substantial underestimation in previous estimates. Geographically, the semi-arid zone has the largest share of CPIC, covering 9.27 ± 0.29 Mha (49.28% of the total), followed by the arid zone (4.69 ± 0.20 Mha, 24.95%) and humid zone (2.99 ± 0.22 Mha, 15.92%). Further analysis indicates that most CPIC is distributed in aquifers with limited underwater recharge. Approximately 15.25 ± 0.87 Mha (82.04%) of CPIC areas are located in regions with recharge rates below 100 mm/year, of which 9.97 ± 0.48 Mha (53.62% of total CPIC) fall within extremely low recharge zones (<20 mm/year). These findings provide an essential foundation for further research on irrigation-groundwater interactions and sustainable policymaking about agricultural development and water usage. Our GCMap inventory is publicly available in an online repository at: https://doi.org/10.12436/GCMap.62.20250711 .

title: GeoPhysAdapter: Scale-matched geophysical adaptation for cross-domain landslide mapping with vision foundation models
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Newly triggered landslides rarely carry immediate annotations, so cross-domain transferability determines the value of landslide mapping for emergency response and regional risk assessment. Vision foundation models have strengthened representational transfer, yet on unseen regions, events, and sources they still generate high-confidence false alarms. Terrain, material, and rainfall triggering can constrain such errors, but their supports are local, regional, and event-scale, so resampling onto a 10 m grid misaligns them with the segmentation decision unit and compounds the uncertain geographic context problem (UGCoP). We propose GeoPhysAdapter, which anchors on a frozen vision foundation model, restricts terrain, material, and triggering to dense spatial guidance, regional modulation, and event-timing forcing, and applies bounded adaptation at two decision units, the pixel and the candidate landslide body, reverting exactly to the visual prediction where support is insufficient. On an event-isolated PILD dataset of four public sources, 55 global landslide events, and 7890 test samples, 70.3% of cross-domain false-positive mass lies in near-pure spurious bodies of median equivalent diameter 207 m, matching coarse-prior support rather than the pixel. Pixel-level adaptation removes a net 507,817 erroneous pixels, reducing error by 7.76%, whereas raising the decision unit to the candidate body, under identical samples, anchor, and baseline, increases error reduction to 23.99% and improves IoU by a relative 14.2%. The gain decreases monotonically with terrain displacement, exceeds a strong optical control of spectral change and visual confidence alone by 0.019 IoU, remains positive across five vision anchors, and survives a pre-registered re-execution with a 20.61% error reduction. The binding constraint is therefore the match between the native scale of physical priors and the operative decision unit, not denser physical stacking. Data and code are publicly available at https://github.com/Liu-Zhihang/geophysadapter .

title: Cross-sensor continual maritime object recognition via spectral shift modulation in heterogeneous infrared–visible UAV imagery
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Multi-modal maritime object recognition is pivotal for UAV-assisted search and rescue. However, large-scale multi-platform UAV deployments inevitably encounter heterogeneous infrared sensors with diverse spectral response functions, leading to non-stationary multi-modal distributions and severe dynamic spectral shifts across successive multi-platform UAV deployment phases. Existing continual learning paradigms typically focus on mitigating catastrophic forgetting via memory replay, but overlook the sensor-specific biases inherent in spectral variations. Such biases induce negative transfer and performance degradation, as the model fails to decouple stable object features from dynamic spectral fluctuations. To address these challenges, we propose C3SM, a cross-sensor spectral shift modulation framework. The core of C3SM is a design-inspired spectral shift parsing prior that decouples sensor-specific spectral responses from sensor-invariant structural cues. By anchoring the fusion features to a structure-consistent reference space within the spatial-frequency domain, the proposed prior quantifies the cross-sensor discrepancy into a spectral shift index. Leveraging this proxy index, C3SM integrates a prior-guided cross-sensor memory modulation module. This module stabilizes the continual learning trajectory by adaptively suppressing unreliable high-shift memory experiences. Furthermore, a shift-robust contrastive learning strategy enforces feature alignment across spectral shift clusters, ensuring the capture of robust cross-sensor correlations. Extensive evaluations on the UAVSensorCL dataset across four heterogeneous sensors illustrate that C3SM achieves a 48.88% mAP at 7.15 FPS, outperforming state-of-the-art CODA-Prompt-PL (45.92% mAP) and ER-PL (45.09% mAP). By mitigating spectral interference, C3SM provides a robust baseline for maritime object recognition across dynamic environments. The dataset and code are available at https://github.com/Dingyuan-Chen/C3SM .

title: Integrating multi-source physical knowledge into deep learning for satellite soil moisture downscaling
abstract: Fine-resolution soil moisture (SM) is essential for understanding land–atmosphere interactions and managing hydrological hazards at local scales. Passive microwave remote sensing provides reliable SM observations but is limited by its coarse spatial resolution. Spatial downscaling offers an important means of addressing this limitation. However, many existing downscaling methods either rely on physical models with over-simplifications of soil hydrological knowledge, or data-driven models (particularly Deep Learning, DL) that lack interpretability, while current physics-guided DL approaches often emphasize a limited number of physical relationships or constraints. In response, this study proposes a framework to integrate multi-source physical knowledge into DL for satellite SM downscaling. Specifically, the framework incorporates physically informed drivers, a DisPATCh-informed physical regression branch, a hydrologically motivated consistency loss, and a constrained SM boundary loss, while using a gating module to adaptively fuse physically guided and data-driven representations. Evaluations based on in-situ and aircraft SM observations, together with coarse-scale consistency checks against SMAP SM, show that the proposed framework can effectively downscale SMAP SM from 9 km to 500 m. Using region-specific models across ten environmentally diverse regions, MPhy achieved station-averaged Pearson’s R and ubRMSE values of 0.76 and 0.05 m3/m3, respectively; the corresponding values for the pure-DL baseline Dens were 0.68 and 0.06 m3/m3. Detailed experiments in WGEW further showed that MPhy generally performed better than the pure-DL baseline, DisPATCh, single-physics-informed models, and selected conventional machine-learning methods. Overall, the results support improved physical plausibility and convergence efficiency, as well as framework robustness across the evaluated environments.

title: Adaptive smooth constrained stereo matching and disparity refinement for satellite DSM generation
abstract: High-resolution satellite images often exhibit substantial geometric and radiometric differences, making it difficult for conventional stereo matching methods to achieve high matching accuracy while suppressing noise and preserving object boundaries. To address this issue, this study improves both stereo matching and disparity post-processing in the satellite digital surface model (DSM) generation workflow. First, within the semi-global matching (SGM) framework, a mixed matching cost is constructed by combining the Census transform and gradient descriptors. Image gradients and edge cues extracted by a pretrained PiDiNet are then incorporated to adaptively control the strength of the smoothness constraint during cost aggregation, thereby improving matching reliability while balancing noise suppression and disparity-boundary preservation. Second, we propose a disparity post-processing method that combines improved weighted least-squares disparity refinement with matching-cost-based disparity fusion. The method first dynamically adjusts the smoothing weights to reduce texture-copying artifacts and edge blurring and then fuses disparity using matching costs to alleviate staircase artifacts caused by excessive smoothing. Experiments were conducted on ZY3-02 and WorldView-3 satellite imagery, with SGM, S2P-HD, Agisoft Metashape software, guided aggregation net, and FoundationStereo included for comparison. Across three test scenes dominated by urban and agricultural areas, the proposed method increased the proportion of pixels with absolute elevation errors below 2 m by an average of 4.12 percentage points and reduced RMSE by an average of 0.11 m compared with standard SGM. Qualitative results further show that the proposed method effectively suppresses noise in relatively flat regions while preserving building boundaries.

title: A large-scale spatiotemporal NDVI prediction method coupling multivariable constraints and structured modeling
abstract: Accurate prediction of vegetation dynamics is essential for understanding terrestrial ecosystems carbon and water cycles. However, existing Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) prediction methods are limited in their ability to represent spatiotemporal heterogeneity and nonlinear interactions among multiple driving variables, which restrict predictive accuracy and extrapolation performance at large scales. To address these limitations, this study proposed a structured large-scale NDVI spatiotemporal prediction method incorporating multivariable constraints (MCS-LSTP) to characterize vegetation dynamics in complex and heterogeneous environments. MCS-LSTP incorporates multiple key driving variables and enhances the comprehensive representation of complex spatiotemporal dependencies and spatial heterogeneity through homogeneous spatial unit partitioning, unit-level temporal modeling, and continuous surface reconstruction. Results showed that MCS-LSTP model exhibited superior performance in terms of stability and prediction accuracy when compared to AutoRegressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA), Random Forest (RF), and Transformer models. The mean Population Stability Index (PSI) reached 0.0572, with 98.7% of prediction units exhibiting PSI values below 0.1, indicating no significant deviation between the observed and simulated NDVI values. The average R2 and RMSE on the test set were 0.8551 and 0.2171, respectively. Furthermore, MCS-LSTP accurately reproduced seasonal NDVI fluctuations and meridional spatial gradients, with particularly high agreement between simulated and reference values during the growing season. This study provides a robust and scalable solution for large-scale NDVI spatiotemporal prediction and offers critical technical support for ecological risk assessment in the Yellow River Basin and other ecologically vulnerable regions.

title: Bottlenecked semantic compression by representation reconstruction
abstract: Vision Transformers incur high computational costs when processing long visual token sequences. Existing reduction methods typically rank tokens independently and discard those deemed unimportant or redundant. We propose a reconstruction-guided framework for visual token condensation (ReConV), which summarizes the complete visual sequence with a compact Summary Bank (SMB) and retains tokens whose information is not adequately captured by the SMB, as indicated by their reconstruction residuals. At each compression layer, a lightweight position-conditioned decoder reconstructs the current tokens, leaving shared information compressed in the SMB while explicitly preserving poorly reconstructed details. Experiments on image classification and multimodal understanding demonstrate favorable performance-efficiency trade-offs: ReConV surpasses the uncompressed baseline with 48\% fewer GMACs on ImageNet and enables reusable image-level representations for efficient multi-turn inference. Code is available at TokenDrop.

title: Extinction by non-spherical particles with the Nanoparticle Transition Matrix Code: perspectives for interstellar medium and exoplanetary atmospheres
abstract: The Transition Matrix formalism (T-matrix) offers an optimal solution to the problem of radiation scattering and absorption by particles characterized by a high degree of chemical and structural complexity. However, its application to particle models composed by large numbers of constituents has been classically limited by the substantial computational burden of the method. As a consequence, the investigation of light scattering and absorption processes, in cases where particle asymmetry and non-homogeneity play an important role, typically need to rely on simplifying assumptions which affect the correct interpretation of transmission spectra and extinction curves. This problem has a huge impact on many fields of scientific application. In particular, it has a critical role in astrophysics, because the ability to model highly non homogeneous particles is a fundamental requirement to understand the role of extinction in different phases of the interstellar medium (ISM), as well as to probe the physics of light transmission in planetary atmospheres within the Solar System and beyond. In this work we describe the application of a new implementation of the T-matrix formalism, based on the framework originally developed by Borghese, Denti & Saija and named Nano-particle Transition Matrix code, which leverages the power of modern hardware architectures to reduce the computational costs related to the solution of relevant particle models for the investigation of dust in the ISM and of hot-Jupyter class planets atmospheric aerosols. This new implementation of the T-matrix formalism can handle calculations of increasing complexity with a direct impact in the interpretation of the transmission spectra of transiting exoplanets produced by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and of those expected from the Atmospheric Remote-sensing Infrared Exoplanet Large survey (ARIEL).

title: Mining Cross-Modal Perception Gaps in Autonomous Driving: When Camera and LiDAR Disagree
abstract: Multi-modal fusion for 3D object detection assumes that cameras and LiDAR are broadly complementary. In practice, how much each modality is trusted at a given location is decided by learned weights that are neither characterized nor auditable. We label every ground-truth object by which modalities detected it, then mine the resulting 0.4M-object database across nuScenes, KITTI, and Waymo. Because the patterns shift with distance from the ego vehicle, we read the mined model through Spatially Stratified Feature Attribution (SSFA), which conditions Shapley attribution on distance zones and exposes structure that global attribution averages away. Three assumptions built into the current fusion design do not hold. The modality-preference boundary tracks the object itself: a traffic cone is nearly six times as likely as a truck to be seen by the camera alone (16.8% vs. 2.9%), regardless of range. Camera-only detections peak at 10-30 m, inside the band usually ceded to LiDAR, and fall away on either side. The drivers of failure are not additive either: the distance - density interaction alone outweighs the entire main effect of viewing direction. We further find that modality dominance is directionally non-stationary, with objects behind the vehicle being markedly more LiDAR-dominant than those in front. We compile the mined structure into a Modality Reliability Map and inject it into four pretrained fusion detectors through a lightweight attention layer. This improves performance by up to 1.3 mean Average Precision (mAP) while fine-tuning under 4% of their parameters in 2-3 GPU-hours. Our work lifts reliability out of the weights and treats it as a quantity that can be examined before deployment. That is what a safety measure for multi-modal perception must rest on.

title: From Parallel to Sequential: Small-Batch Noise Restores Simplicity Bias of Muon
abstract: Simplicity bias, which can arise from sequential feature learning during training, has been proposed as a general explanation for the success of deep learning. An important driver of this phenomenon is saddle-to-saddle behavior, in which the gradient flow trajectory remains close to a sequence of saddle manifolds while learning one feature at a time. However, Muon, a state-of-the-art optimizer based on spectral descent, does not exhibit such dynamics in the full-batch setting and instead learns features in parallel. How is it then that Muon is so successful in deep learning settings? We show that stochastic gradient noise fundamentally changes this behavior: small-batch noise restores sequential feature learning, providing a mechanism for simplicity bias that is absent from full-batch Muon. We explain this transition through stochastic smoothing of the spectral descent operator underlying Muon. When gradients are small relative to the noise scale, the expected spectral update becomes approximately proportional to the actual gradient, which restores gradient-flow-like dynamics. We formalize this mechanism for deep linear models by deriving the effective continuous dynamics of noisy spectral descent. Experiments on low-rank matrix reconstruction, vision transformers, and large language models (LLMs) support these findings.

title: Growing to See: Efficient Pretraining of Self-Supervised Vision Transformers
abstract: Progressive depth growth builds large networks by starting with shallow models and inserting layers during training. Recent advances in large language models have renewed interest in this longstanding approach, demonstrating benefits for training efficiency and reasoning alongside changes in internal computations. However, how growing affects representation quality and computational patterns in self-supervised vision transformers remains unclear. In this work, we systematically investigate progressive depth growth in two popular self-supervised families, namely masked autoencoders (MAE) and DINOv3, and analyze how growing affects downstream performance, intermediate representations, and internal computations. Across global and dense tasks, we show that growing improves downstream performance while reducing training FLOPs by 13.9--24.8%, with ImageNet linear-probe accuracy gains of up to 3.36 percentage points. Growing also improves downstream performance at intermediate layers and reshapes internal computational patterns, introducing recurring alternations between global and localized attention in MAE and earlier local-to-global attention progression in self-distilled DINOv3. Together, these findings establish progressive depth growth as an effective and efficient pretraining strategy for improving downstream performance across global and dense visual tasks with less computation, and advance our understanding of how growing shapes visual computation.

title: An updated view of Jupiter's UV main auroral emission: large-scale analysis of UV and particle data from Juno's first 60 orbits
abstract: The properties and origins of Jupiter's UV main auroral emission are, at present, not yet fully understood, particularly the extent to which its two distinct zones, the Zone-I and Zone-II aurora, originate from a common source. In this work, remote-sensing and in-situ data from the Juno spacecraft are used to investigate and produce maps of the average properties of the main emission over Juno's first 60 orbits. It is found that the peak in mean energy of electrons precipitating in the main emission is consistently poleward of the energy-flux (or brightness) peak, in both hemispheres and at all local times, and is co-located with the statistical location of the Zone-II aurora. Evidence is presented that the flux-energy relationship of the main emission is adequately characterised by theoretical power laws describing electron acceleration from quasi-static potentials or Alfvénic turbulence and that it shows a modulation with ionospheric electron density consistent with theoretical predictions. Finally, the average energy spectra of precipitating electrons in the Zone-I aurora remain power-law-like between an energy flux of 1 and 100 mW m$^{-2}$, whereas the average Zone-II spectra develop a distinct ``plateau'' or ``flattop'' shape beyond an energy flux of $\sim$5 mW m$^{-2}$.
